q01.key_idea: Move the kangaroo and the rabbit one turn at a time.
steps: The kangaroo starts at the bottom. The rabbit starts on step 10.
Turn 1: the kangaroo jumps up 3 to step 3. The rabbit hops down 2 to step 8.
Turn 2: the kangaroo jumps up 3 more to step 6. The rabbit hops down 2 more to step 6.
Now they are both on step 6. They meet!

choice_feedback.A: The kangaroo is on step 3 after one jump, but the rabbit is still up on step 8.
choice_feedback.B: The kangaroo stops on 3, 6, 9. It never stops on step 4.
choice_feedback.C: The kangaroo stops on 3, 6, 9 and the rabbit on 8, 6, 4. Nobody stops on step 5.
choice_feedback.E: The rabbit stops on 8, 6, 4. It never stops on step 7.

q02.key_idea: Each piece must line up with the part of the kangaroo next to it.
steps: Piece 3 has the head, so it goes on top.
Piece 1 has the body and the feet, so it goes right under the head.
Piece 2 has the tail. The tail sticks out from the back of the body, so piece 2 goes to the left of piece 1.
Piece 4 goes above the tail, next to the head. Top row: 4, 3. Bottom row: 2, 1.

choice_feedback.B: The head ends up above the tail instead of above the body.
choice_feedback.C: The head ends up at the bottom.
choice_feedback.D: The tail ends up on the far right, so it does not touch the back of the body.
choice_feedback.E: The head is above the tail and the tail is away from the body.

q03.key_idea: The parts of the castle we can still see must match the castle exactly.
steps: Maria stands in front of the castle, so her face covers part of it in the photo.
The parts we can still see must have the same towers, in the same order, as the castle.
Picture E keeps the tall tower in its place, and Maria's face covers part of the right side.

choice_feedback.A: Compare this castle with the picture bump by bump.
choice_feedback.B: Compare this castle with the picture bump by bump.
choice_feedback.C: This castle has no tall tower in it.
choice_feedback.D: Compare this castle with the picture bump by bump.

review.note: Key E is confirmed by the official CMKC 2020 answer table. Steps and feedback for A, B, D are method-only; a worked explanation of why D does not fit is still needed.

q04.key_idea: Find the group of 5 animals that keeps repeating.
steps: The animals come in this order: mouse, snail, bird, bird, frog. Then the order starts again.
The picture shows mouse, snail, bird, bird, frog, then mouse, snail, bird, bird, frog, then a mouse.
After the mouse comes the snail, and after the snail comes a bird.

choice_feedback.A: The frog and the mouse came just before. Next is the snail.
choice_feedback.B: The two birds come after the snail, so the snail must come first.
choice_feedback.C: A bird and a frog come later, after the snail.
choice_feedback.D: The mouse was just pulled out. Next come the snail and a bird.

q05.key_idea: Each shape on the edge of a square is cut in half, and the other half is on the next square.
steps: Look at the half shapes that touch the empty square: above it, left of it, right of it and below it.
The missing piece must finish every one of those half shapes.
Check each piece edge by edge to see which one finishes all four shapes.

choice_feedback.A: Check each edge of this piece against the square next to it.
choice_feedback.B: Check each edge of this piece against the square next to it.
choice_feedback.D: Check each edge of this piece against the square next to it.
choice_feedback.E: Check each edge of this piece against the square next to it.

review.note: Key C is confirmed by the official CMKC 2020 answer table; the blind solve (B) was wrong. Steps and feedback are method-only and still need a worked explanation of why C fits.

q06.key_idea: Work out every square, then shade the ones that make 13.
steps: The squares that make 13 are the top right one and the bottom right one.
So Tara shades the whole right side.

choice_feedback.A: 8 + 4 is 12, not 13, so the top left square stays white.
choice_feedback.C: 8 + 4 is 12, not 13, so the top left square stays white.
choice_feedback.D: 8 + 4 is 12, not 13, and 6 + 7 is 13, so the bottom right square is shaded too.
choice_feedback.E: 19 - 6 is also 13, so the top right square is shaded too.

q07.key_idea: Both dogs walk the same distance, so they meet halfway along the path.
steps: Count the path in grid sides. From P it goes up 4, right 1, down 2, right 1, up 2, right 1, down 3, left 2, down 1, right 3, up 4.
That is 24 sides in all. Half of 24 is 12.
Count 12 sides from P: you pass A at 9, B at 10 and C at 11, and you reach D at 12.
Both dogs walk 12 sides, so they meet at D.

choice_feedback.A: A is only 9 sides from P. Halfway is 12.
choice_feedback.B: B is 10 sides from P. Halfway is 12.
choice_feedback.C: C is 11 sides from P, one short of halfway.
choice_feedback.E: E is 13 sides from P, one past halfway.

q08.key_idea: Find the smallest number of apples that 5 children can share equally.
steps: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. 12 is not in the list, so 12 apples can't be shared equally.
The next number after 12 is 15.
15 - 12 = 3, so Grandmother needs 3 more apples. Then each child gets 3.

choice_feedback.A: 12 apples can't be split into 5 equal groups.
choice_feedback.B: With 1 more there are 13 apples, and 13 can't be shared equally by 5.
choice_feedback.C: With 2 more there are 14 apples, and 14 can't be shared equally by 5.
choice_feedback.E: With 4 more there are 16 apples, and 16 can't be shared equally by 5.

q09.key_idea: Count every cube, including the ones hiding behind or under others.
steps: A has 5 cubes. B has 5 cubes.
C has 7 cubes. D has 6 cubes.
E has 6 cubes on the bottom, in two rows of 3, and 2 more stacked on top: 8 cubes.
8 is the most.

choice_feedback.C: C has 7 cubes. E has one more.
choice_feedback.D: D has 6 cubes. Look for the cubes hiding at the back of E.

q10.key_idea: Add up the big flower, then find what the small flower is missing.
steps: Small flower: 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20, plus the hidden petal.
Both flowers must make 25. 20 + 5 = 25, so the hidden petal is 5.

q11.key_idea: All six numbers add up to 21. The colored squares use up 20 of it.
steps: The blue squares make 10 and the yellow squares make 10. 10 + 10 = 20.
Only the ? square is left. 21 - 20 = 1.
For example: yellow 4 and 6, blue 2, 3 and 5, and 1 in the ? square.

choice_feedback.B: If ? were 2, the colored squares would add up to 19, not 20.
choice_feedback.C: If ? were 3, the colored squares would add up to 18, not 20.
choice_feedback.D: If ? were 4, the colored squares would add up to 17, not 20.
choice_feedback.E: If ? were 5, the colored squares would add up to 16, not 20.

q12.key_idea: Follow each band all the way around so you count it only once.
steps: Put your finger on one band and follow it all the way around until you come back to the start.
Mark that band, then pick a band you have not followed yet.
Keep going until every band is counted. There are 6 bands.

choice_feedback.A: Some bands cross each other. Follow each one all the way around.
choice_feedback.B: A band may be hiding behind another one.
choice_feedback.D: You may have counted one band twice.
choice_feedback.E: You may have counted some bands twice.

review.note: Key C (6 bands) is confirmed by the official CMKC 2020 answer table. The steps describe the tracing method; a band-by-band description is still needed.

q13.key_idea: When one train's car numbers go down, the other train's go up by the same amount.
steps: The top train's cars count 1, 2, 3 to the right. The bottom train's cars count 1, 2, 3 to the left.
Car 19 is opposite car 19. Car 12 is 7 cars to the left of car 19, because 19 - 7 = 12.
On the bottom train, moving 7 cars to the left makes the number go up by 7: 19 + 7 = 26.
So car 12 is opposite car 26.

choice_feedback.A: As you move left, the other train's numbers get bigger, not smaller.
choice_feedback.B: The trains line up at car 19, not at car 12.
choice_feedback.C: 21 is only 2 cars away from 19. We need to move 7 cars.
choice_feedback.E: 31 is the last car, 12 cars away from 19. We need to move 7 cars.

q14.key_idea: An arrow always points to someone shorter.
steps: Look for the person with no arrow going out. That person is not taller than anyone.
A, B, D, E and F all have an arrow going out.
C has no arrow going out, and arrows from D and F point to C.
C is the shortest.

choice_feedback.A: A has an arrow to D, so A is taller than D.
choice_feedback.B: B has arrows to A and F, so B is tall.
choice_feedback.D: D has an arrow to C, so D is taller than C.
choice_feedback.E: E has an arrow to D, so E is taller than D.

q15.key_idea: Opposite faces always add up to the same total.
steps: 4, 8 and 5 touch each other, so each of them has its own opposite face.
Try 6 opposite 5. The total is 5 + 6 = 11.
Then 4 needs 7 (4 + 7 = 11) and 8 needs 3 (8 + 3 = 11).
The numbers 5, 6, 4, 7, 8 and 3 are all different. It works!

choice_feedback.A: 5 + 3 = 8, so 8 would need 0 opposite it, and 0 is not allowed.
choice_feedback.B: The numbers must all be different, and 5 is already used.
choice_feedback.D: 5 + 7 = 12, so 4 would need 8, but 8 is already on another face.
choice_feedback.E: 5 + 9 = 14, so 4 would need 10, which is too big.

q16.key_idea: Work backwards from the end, undoing one step at a time.
steps: At the end, John and Olivia each have 4 sweets.
In the last step Olivia doubled John's sweets. So before that John had 2, and Olivia had 4 + 2 = 6.
In the first step John doubled Olivia's sweets. So before that Olivia had 3, and John had 2 + 3 = 5.
John started with 5 sweets.

choice_feedback.A: If John had 6, Olivia had 2. They would end with 8 and 0.
choice_feedback.C: If John had 4, Olivia had 4. They would end with 0 and 8.
choice_feedback.D: If John had 3, Olivia had 5. John can't give 5 sweets when he has only 3.
choice_feedback.E: If John had 2, Olivia had 6. John can't give 6 sweets when he has only 2.

q17.key_idea: Write all the digits out, cross some out, and find the middle one.
steps: Cross out every 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9.
What is left is 2 4 6 8 0 2 4 6 8. That is 9 digits.
The middle one is the 5th digit, which is 0.

choice_feedback.B: 2 is the 1st and the 6th digit, not the middle one.
choice_feedback.C: 4 is the 2nd and the 7th digit, not the middle one.
choice_feedback.D: 6 is the 3rd and the 8th digit, not the middle one.
choice_feedback.E: 8 is the 4th and the 9th digit, not the middle one.

q18.key_idea: Each fold turns the paper over, so the digit turns too.
steps: Follow the square with the 2 through the first fold.
Then follow it through the second fold.
Each fold flips the square over, so the 2 is turned around after both folds, like in picture D.

choice_feedback.A: This is how the 2 would look if it never turned over.
choice_feedback.B: Follow the 2 through both folds to see which way it turns.
choice_feedback.C: Follow the 2 through both folds to see which way it turns.
choice_feedback.E: Follow the 2 through both folds to see which way it turns.

review.note: Key D is confirmed by the official CMKC 2020 answer table. Steps and feedback are method-only and still need a worked fold-by-fold explanation.
